The head-side changed range 1208-1209 lies inside the supplied base text; it appears to be the `--kv-quantization` and `--kv-checkpoint-quantization` rows. I could not see the head lines, so I could not confirm exactly what changed there. Based on the base text at lines 1208-1209 and the patch description, those rows are documentation of existing benchmark options.

I found no security-relevant behavior change. The supplied text contains no code, config defaults, endpoint changes, or changes to authorization, App Attest, key custody, or cache storage.

I checked the cache-related documentation against T-041. It states that benchmark runs keep prefix caches off and that the checkpoint quantization request does not enable caching. That is consistent with T-041. The SSD cache posture is also unchanged: the 30-minute TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE as the kill switch, and HMAC-keyed names. The base text mentions Team ID, the token path, and the App Attest worker env passthrough. These are pre-existing, unchanged documentation.

One limit: the patch excerpt is truncated and the head text is not supplied. A new benchmark concurrency mode may add local runtime behavior, such as concurrent engine use or memory pressure. That behavior is outside the supplied evidence, and benchmarks run locally under operator control, so it is not a finding. If the code PR introduces RuntimeConcurrencyBenchmark, it should be reviewed separately for prompt or log exposure and resource exhaustion.
